arxiv-2008-00494.title: Partially Coherent Direct Sum Channels
arxiv-2008-00494.creator: Stefano Chessa, Vittorio Giovannetti
arxiv-2008-00494.description: Abstract We introduce Partially Coherent Direct Sum (PCDS) quantum channels, as a generalization of the already known Direct Sum quantum channels. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions to identify the subset of those maps which are degradable, and provide a simplified expression for their quantum capacities.

arxiv-2202-00612.title: Similarity Learning based Few Shot Learning for ECG Time Series Classification
arxiv-2202-00612.creator: Priyanka Gupta, Sathvik Bhaskarpandit, Manik Gupta
arxiv-2202-00612.description: Abstract Using deep learning models to classify time series data generated from the Internet of Things (IoT) devices requires a large amount of labeled data. However, due to constrained resources available in IoT devices, it is often difficult to accommodate training using large data sets.

arxiv-2202-08986.title: The Fibonacci Sequence is Normal Base 10 Thanks: Second author partially supported by Simons Foundation grant number 359721.
arxiv-2202-08986.creator: Brennan Benfield, Michelle Manes
arxiv-2202-08986.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Brennan Benfield, Michelle Manes. In this paper, we show that the concatenation of the Fibonacci sequence is normal in base 10 10 , meaning every string of a given length, k k , occurs as frequently as every other string of length k k (there are as many 1 1 ’s as 2 2 ’s and as many 704 704 ’s and 808 808 ’s). Although we know that almost every number is normal, we can name very few of them.

arxiv-2211-06214.title: Linear Fault Estimators for Nonlinear Systems: An Ultra-Local Model Design footnoteinfo This publication is part of the project Digital Twin project 4.3 with project number P18-03 of the research programme Perspectief which is (mainly) financed by the Dutch Research Council (NWO).
arxiv-2211-06214.creator: Farhad Ghanipoor, Carlos Murguia, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani, Nathan van de Wouw
arxiv-2211-06214.description: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of robust process and sensor fault reconstruction for nonlinear systems. The proposed method augments the system dynamics with an approximated internal linear model of the combined contribution of known nonlinearities and unknown faults – leading to an approximated linear model in the augmented state.

arxiv-2301-00513.title: Holographic entanglement entropy and subregion complexity for excited states of holographic superconductors
arxiv-2301-00513.creator: Dong Wang 1 , Xiongying Qiao 1 , Mengjie Wang 1 , Qiyuan Pan 1,3 , Chuyu Lai 2 , and Jiliang Jing 1,3
arxiv-2301-00513.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dong Wang 1 , Xiongying Qiao 1 , Mengjie Wang 1 , Qiyuan Pan 1,3 , Chuyu Lai 2 , and Jiliang Jing 1,3. Abstract We investigate the holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and the holographic subregion complexity (HSC) for holographic superconductors, both in the Einstein and in the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravitational theories.

arxiv-2305-18479.title: FMM-X3D: FPGA-based modeling and mapping of X3D for Human Action Recognition
arxiv-2305-18479.creator: Petros Toupas, Christos-Savvas Bouganis, Dimitrios Tzovaras
arxiv-2305-18479.description: Abstract 3D Convolutional Neural Networks are gaining increasing attention from researchers and practitioners and have found applications in many domains, such as surveillance systems, autonomous vehicles, human monitoring systems, and video retrieval. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by their high computational and memory requirements, especially when resource-constrained systems are targeted.

arxiv-2405-10281.title: The dynamics and electromagnetic signatures of accretion in unequal mass binary black hole inspirals 2024 The dynamics and electromagnetic signatures of accretion in unequal mass binary black hole inspirals – References
arxiv-2405-10281.creator: Madeline Clyburn & Jonathan Zrake
arxiv-2405-10281.description: Abstract We present a theoretical study of the gravitational wave (GW) driven inspirals of accreting black hole binaries with mass M = 10 7 ​ M ⊙ M=10^{7}M_{\odot} and mass ratios between 10 − 3 10^{-3} and 10 − 1 10^{-1} .

arxiv-2505-12642.title: Two out of Three (ToT): using self-consistency to make robust predictions
arxiv-2505-12642.creator: Jung H. Lee, Sujith Vijayan
arxiv-2505-12642.description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) can automatically construct intelligent agents, deep neural networks (alternatively, DL models), that can outperform humans in certain tasks. However, the operating principles of DL remain poorly understood, making its decisions incomprehensible. As a result, it poses a great risk to deploy DL in high-stakes domains in which mistakes or errors may lead to critical consequences.

arxiv-2507-09947.title: Modeling Cholera Dynamics with Vaccination as the Control Strategy and Seasonal-forcing Transmission
arxiv-2507-09947.creator: Eric Herrison Gyamfi
arxiv-2507-09947.description: Abstract This study presents a seasonally forced S ​ V ​ I ​ R ​ - ​ B SVIR\text{-}B cholera model that incorporates imperfect vaccination as a control strategy. The model captures the temporal dynamics of susceptible, vaccinated, infected, and recovered individuals, as well as the environmental pathogen concentration.

arxiv-2509-21569.title: A Markovian approach to N N -photon correlations beyond the quantum regression theorem
arxiv-2509-21569.creator: Mateusz Salamon, Oliver Dudgeon, Ahsan Nazir, Jake Iles-Smith
arxiv-2509-21569.description: Abstract Multi-photon correlations from quantum emitters coupled to vibrational environments lie beyond the reach of standard tools such as the quantum regression theorem (QRT). Here, we introduce a Markovian framework for computing frequency-resolved N N -photon correlation functions that overcomes this limitation.

arxiv-2511-14030.title: Training-free Detection of AI-generated images via Cropping Robustness
arxiv-2511-14030.creator: Sungik Choi, Hankook Lee, Moontae Lee
arxiv-2511-14030.description: Abstract AI-generated image detection has become crucial with the rapid advancement of vision-generative models. Instead of training detectors tailored to specific datasets, we study a training-free approach leveraging self-supervised models without requiring prior data knowledge. These models, pre-trained with augmentations like RandomResizedCrop , learn to produce consistent representations across varying resolutions.

arxiv-2601-16854.title: Stochastic Analysis of Fifth-Order KdV Soliton in Damping Regime and Reduction to Painlevé Second Equation
arxiv-2601-16854.creator: Irfan Mahmood, Adeena Iqbal, Sohail Mumtaz, [1ex] Center for High Energy Physics, University of the PunjabQuaid-e-Azam Campus, Lahore 54590, Pakistan
arxiv-2601-16854.description: Abstract This work presents a stochastic analysis of fifth-order KdV soliton momentum distribution in a damping regime. An explicit representation of the soliton momentum associated with amplitude variation is derived in terms of a random time function in the presence of dissipation.

pmc-10597079.title: Regional health and social inequalities in Bulgaria
pmc-10597079.creator: D Tsanova, S Georgieva, M Kamburova, E Mineva-Dimitrova, B Ivanova, A Seizov, T Vitkova
pmc-10597079.description: BackgroundThe administrative division of Bulgaria divides it into 28 regions, which differ significantly in terms of both socioeconomic development and a number of demographic indicators. The death rate is an indicator according to which our country has been at the top of the world rankings for several years.

pmc-11338332.title: Post laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy portal vein thrombosis with venous mesenteric ischemia: a case report with literature review
pmc-11338332.creator: Hamid Abdulla Al Wadaani, Sarah Al Omar, Jawaher AlRaihan, Jawad S Alnajjar, Mohamed Elserougi, Hussain Al Jabran
pmc-11338332.description: Saudi Arabia’s obesity prevalence is 19.2% among men and 21.4% among women. Treatment includes lifestyle modifications, medication, and bariatric surgery. Procedures reach up to 1200 annually in our center. Porto-mesenteric venous thrombosis associated with venous mesenteric ischemia and bowel necrosis is a rare complication that necessitates an early workup and management. A 29-year-old Saudi male underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.

pmc-12386503.title: Vitamin D as an Epigenetic Regulator: A Hypothetical Mechanism for Cancer Prevention via Inhibition of Oncogenic lncRNA HOTAIR
pmc-12386503.creator: Samuel Trujano-Camacho, Ángel Pulido-Capiz, Victor García-González, Eduardo López-Urrutia, Carlos Pérez-Plasencia, Marisabel Mecca
pmc-12386503.description: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, arising from a complex interplay of genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors. Although the role of micronutrients in cancer development has received limited attention, growing evidence suggests that vitamins, particularly vitamin D, may influence oncogenic pathways.

pmc-12428807.title: The Interplay Between Oxidative Stress and Lipid Composition in Obesity-Induced Inflammation: Antioxidants as Therapeutic Agents in Metabolic Diseases
pmc-12428807.creator: Mariló Olivares-Vicente, María Herranz-López, Guan-Jhong Huang
pmc-12428807.description: Adipose tissue functions not only as a lipid storage depot but also as an active endocrine organ that regulates key physiological processes. In obesity, oxidative stress disrupts the molecular pathways for adipose tissue homeostasis, triggering chronic inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and metabolic disorders.

pmc-12491461.title: Acoustic water display
pmc-12491461.creator: Félix Sisombat, Thibaut Devaux, Samuel Callé, Jere Hyvönen, Axi Holmström, Ari Salmi, Lionel Haumesser
pmc-12491461.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Cross-boundary communication between media with high impedance mismatch, such as air and water, remains a major challenge for conventional wireless transmission systems. At such interfaces, most of the emitted signal energy is reflected at the media boundaries. Here, we propose a novel display technology for optical information transmission across such an interface, using acoustic radiation pressure to dynamically shape the water–air boundary. The design is based on the combination of spatiotemporal deformations of a water-air interface induced by acoustic radiation pressure.

pmc-12546826.title: AMMI and GGE biplot analysis for seed yield and stability performance of selected buckwheat genotypes under multi-environmental trials
pmc-12546826.creator: Raghav Sood, Gopal Katna, Manoj Negi, Surinder Kumar Kaushik, Gyanendra Pratap Singh, Mohar Singh
pmc-12546826.description: Buckwheat is an underutilized yet nutrient dense crop with immense potential for sustainable agriculture, especially in regions with challenging agroclimatic conditions. This study assessed the yield performance and stability of twenty buckwheat genotypes across two distinct locations over three consecutive years (2022–2024).

pmc-13195430.title: A layered double hydroxide nanocarrier enables YM155 delivery-induced PANoptosis and immunogenic activation in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13195430.creator: Jie Gong, Xianxing Wang, Jiali Yang, Li Tang, Lei Cai, Huaizhi Wang
pmc-13195430.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a highly lethal malignancy due to its intrinsic resistance to apoptosis and limited response to conventional chemotherapy. This therapeutic bottleneck is closely associated with aberrant cell death regulation and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which collectively restrict effective tumor eradication.

pmc-13562681.title: Perioperative myeloid cell remodeling shapes CAR-T cell efficacy in glioblastoma
pmc-13562681.creator: Martin Pedard, Luis Castillo Cantero, Ali Ghasemi, Eliana Marinari, Caterina Mollica, Suzel Davanture, Julie Pernot, Valérie Widmer, Doron Merkler, Kristof Egervari, Karl Schaller, Philippe Bijlenga, Andrea Bartoli, Shahan Momjian, Mikael J Pittet, Valérie Dutoit, Denis Migliorini
pmc-13562681.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that constrains the efficacy of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy. Here, we show that surgical resection in both male mice and human GBM ex vivo induces a rapid and sustained remodeling of the TME, marked by upregulation of TREM2 in myeloid cells followed by emergence of T cell exhaustion-like phenotypes.
